name: Guardian genius crossword No 192
preamble: 27 9 by 24 21 across, 25 down by 1 17 across, 3 15 by 23 32, and 13 by co-authors 12 26 down and 2 30 are all works of fiction with no further definition in the clues. All other clues are normal.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perfect question about fiction finally clear

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows, and nothing else of it
about means going round, so one pair of pieces wraps itself around the other pair

blocks.note: A1 means first-class or perfect, with the 1 written as the letter I
Q is the standard abbreviation for question
the final letter of fiction
a net figure is what you clear after deductions

explanation.surface: A quiz-setter's perfect question about a novel's ending turns out to be easy to answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says this is an author with no definition in the clue: Anne Tiq, said aloud, is antique, the writer of Past It. A1Q goes round N and NET.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble names this pun author as the writer of the themed book Past It, so no clue words define it.

clue.text: Very small bottle containing base, but not oxygen

indicators.note: containing says one word holds the other inside its letters
but not tells us to take something away from the word just before it

blocks.note: so and very are interchangeable intensifiers
a phial is a small glass bottle for medicine
base and foul both mean low or vile
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemistry instruction: a tiny bottle holds an alkaline base, but it must contain no oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble defines this author: Sophia Full sounds like so fearful, co-author of Afraid. Base here means vile, not the chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble names this pun author as co-writer of the themed book Afraid, so no clue words define it.

clue.text: Farm building is sty with piglet on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside keeps only the two outer letters of the word, its first and its last

blocks.note: a grange is a farmhouse with its outbuildings
taken as written, to be rearranged
the first and last letters of piglet

explanation.surface: A farmyard description: the building is a pigsty with a little pig standing outside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble defines this title, Gran Gets Tipsy by Sheri Trifle (sherry trifle). No word signals the rearrangement of IS STY and PT; a sty is a mess, which is the nearest hint.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble names this as a work of fiction, the book written by Sheri Trifle, so no clue words define it.

clue.text: Drink possibly as a joke, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks us to judge the phrase by how it is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: doing something as a joke is doing it in jest

explanation.surface: Someone half-hears a suggestion to drink something for a laugh and asks if they heard right.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or liquid into the body, and drinking is one example of that, hence possibly.

clue.text: Composition ending in disaster, a riot breaks out in the midst of tomfoolery

indicators.note: ending in picks out only the final letter of the word that follows
a riot that breaks out scatters, so these letters are scattered into a new order
in the midst of places the jumbled group right inside the other piece

blocks.note: the two central letters of the ten-letter word tomfoolery
the final letter of disaster
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A news report: a disaster ends in a riot breaking out amid a scene of silly horseplay.
explanation.walkthrough: Composition looks like a description of the chaos, but it is the definition; the middle of tomfoolery is its fifth and sixth letters, two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work for choir, soloists and orchestra, a type of musical composition.

clue.text: Hammer up or hammer down

indicators.note: hammering something beats it out of shape, so the letters are battered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A symmetrical instruction about swinging a hammer upward or bringing it down.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves look like matching phrases, but the first Hammer is the instruction and only the second hammer belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that hammers down falls in torrents, which is what we mean when we say it pours.

clue.text: Yes, pendulum slowing evidently starts to wind up clock

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of each of the words before it
in a down answer, winding up means the letters climb from the bottom, read in reverse

blocks.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A clock owner notices the pendulum slowing, so it is time to wind the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Clock looks like the thing being wound, but it is a slang verb meaning to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock is informal British slang for catch sight of or notice someone, the same meaning as spot or see.

clue.text: Loose women aim to go far beyond Xanadu in the end

indicators.note: in the end keeps only the final letter of each word it governs
beyond places the first group after the letter from the last word

blocks.note: the final letter of Xanadu
the final letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Liberated women set their sights on travelling further than the fabled palace of Xanadu.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose reads as an adjective describing women, but it is a verb, set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmoor a boat is to release it from its moorings, which is to loose or cast it off.

clue.text: See 27
That’s cute on you, I agree

indicators.note: on means placed on top of, so the exclamation is set after the old pronoun

blocks.note: ye is the old form of you
ah is the noise people make at something sweet

explanation.surface: A compliment about an outfit: that looks cute on you, and someone else agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is a casual spoken form of yes, an informal way to signal agreement with someone.

clue.text: Born name, not a married name ultimately

indicators.note: not removes the letters that follow from the word before
ultimately points to the very last letter of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
A as written, and M is the abbreviation for married
the final letter of name

explanation.surface: A note on surnames: a birth name, as opposed to the name taken on marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: NAME loses A and M to leave NE, then gains the last letter of name.
explanation.definitionFit: Née is French for born, used before a married woman's original family surname.

clue.text: School run coming up after short period

indicators.note: coming up, in a word that runs down, means its letters are read upward, back to front
short means cut off the final letter of the word it describes
after puts the turned-round group behind the clipped piece

blocks.note: a term is a period, such as a school term
to school someone is to teach or edify them
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A parent's routine: the school run comes round again after a brief holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble defines this author: Terry Fide sounds like terrified, co-author of Afraid. School is a verb here, not the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble names this pun author as co-writer of the themed book Afraid, so no clue words define it.

clue.text: A tailless fish eaten by tailless dog

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off, for both the fish and the dog
something eaten by another ends up inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a ray is a flat sea fish
Fido is the stock name for a pet dog

explanation.surface: A grim pet-shop scene: a fish with no tail swallowed by a dog that has lost its tail too.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble defines this title, Afraid by Terry Fide and Sophia Full (terrified, so fearful). Tailless applies to both RAY and FIDO.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble names this as a work of fiction by the co-authors, so no words in the clue define it.

clue.text: Considerable weight added to a doctrinal ruling

indicators.note: added to joins the first pieces on in front of the last one

blocks.note: a fat sum is a considerable one
W is the abbreviation for weight
taken as written

explanation.surface: Heavy significance is attached to a religious ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a formal ruling on a point of Islamic law given by a recognised religious authority.

clue.text: See 3
Key fine in fact, the door closes

indicators.note: closes refers to the closing letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: the final letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Someone reassures us the key works fine, since the door does in fact close.
explanation.walkthrough: Key suggests a door key, but it is a computer keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: Enter is the name of the keyboard key pressed to confirm input or start a new line.

clue.text: See 1
Brownish colour for all to see in stick

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word that follows

blocks.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone
to tape something is to stick it

explanation.surface: A brownish colour displayed on a stick for everyone to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Taupe is a greyish-brown shade, named after the French word for mole, whose fur has that hue.

clue.text: Verbal signals in lines

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: cues are signals telling a performer when to act

explanation.surface: Spoken signals given out in lines, perhaps prompts for actors.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines looks like an actor's lines, matching the signals, but it means people waiting in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Queues are rows of people waiting their turn, which Americans call lines.

clue.text: Ruminators, I’m sorry to say, stealing hat from behind

indicators.note: from behind means the word is read starting at its back end
stealing means taking something in and keeping it inside

blocks.note: alas is an expression of regret
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: An apology: some cud-chewing animals sneaked up and snatched a hat from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruminators suggests deep thinkers, but here it means animals that chew the cud.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpacas are South American camelids that chew the cud, so they are ruminating animals.

clue.text: Love child pocketing small gold receptacle at the dentist’s

indicators.note: pocketing means putting something away inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: Cupid, god of love, is pictured as a child
S is the abbreviation for small
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A child born outside marriage slips a bit of gold into their pocket at the dentist's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Love child suggests an illegitimate child, but it is the god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuspidor is a spittoon, the bowl a dental patient spits into after rinsing.

clue.text: See 24
CD lacking with this old band

blocks.note: only the C of this pair is taken as written; the D is read with the next word
read with the D before it, D lacking is a shortage of vitamin D, which causes the bone disease rickets

explanation.surface: A complaint that an old band's CD is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: CD looks like a compact disc, but the C stands alone and D lacking is a disease. The band played behind Buddy Holly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crickets were Buddy Holly's backing group in the 1950s, a rock and roll band from long ago.

clue.text: Boring line on semicircle

indicators.note: on means resting upon, so the railway line comes after the shape

blocks.note: the capital letter D is shaped like a semicircle
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson that consists of a line drawn on a semicircle, which sounds tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry speech or book is dull and uninteresting, the same sense as tedious.

clue.text: Rob following last of ancestors, ageless traditions passed on

indicators.note: last of takes only the closing letter of the next word
ageless means without age, so those three letters are struck out of the following word
following puts the first word after the rest

blocks.note: the final letter of ancestors
heritage is what is handed down from earlier generations
to rifle through something is to search and rob it

explanation.surface: Someone robs an old family of its age-old traditions that had been passed down.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble defines this author: Sheri Trifle sounds like sherry trifle, a British pudding of sponge, sherry, custard and cream, and wrote Gran Gets Tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble names this pun author as the writer of the themed book Gran Gets Tipsy, so no clue words define it.

clue.text: One’s all jittery with ice on river

indicators.note: something jittery is shaking about, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone feels nervous standing on a frozen river.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble defines this author: Elaine Closure sounds like lane closure, the writer of Road Narrows. The Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble names this pun author as the writer of the themed book Road Narrows, so no clue words define it.

clue.text: Man’s arm

blocks.note: first meaning: a playing ... in chess or draughts
second meaning: a gun, in slang

explanation.walkthrough: Man's arm reads as a body part, but man is a chess man and arm is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Chessmen are called pieces, and in slang a piece is a handgun, a weapon or firearm.

clue.text: Where church is for desire?

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about where a church stands, asked out of longing
setter's reading: desire is ITCH, and the church letters CH sit after its first two letters, I and T

explanation.walkthrough: The preamble defines this title, Past It by Anne Tiq (antique). In ITCH, the letters CH come after IT, so church is past it.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble names this as a work of fiction, the book written by Anne Tiq, so no clue words define it.

clue.text: Having guzzled last of butter, womanly figure’s deserted physicist

indicators.note: last of takes only the closing letter of the next word
deserted means the figure has left, so its letters are removed
having guzzled means swallowing something so it sits inside

blocks.note: the final letter of butter
feminine means womanly
nine is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: After eating too much butter, a woman's figure is no longer what it was.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure suggests a woman's shape, but it is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Fermi was the Italian-American scientist who built the first nuclear reactor.

clue.text: See 12
Around back of field, horse darts

indicators.note: back of takes only the final letter of the next word
around means one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat
the final letter of field
arrows is the pub-game slang name for darts

explanation.surface: A horse darts round the far end of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble defines this title, Road Narrows by Elaine Closure (lane closure), a joke on the road sign. Darts is a noun, not the horse's movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble names this as a work of fiction, the book written by Elaine Closure, so no clue words define it.

clue.text: Chest mysterious, not opening

indicators.note: not opening means the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: dark can mean hidden or mysterious

explanation.surface: A mysterious chest that will not open.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's lid that will not open is really the instruction to remove a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ark is an old word for a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant.

clue.text: Among gangsters, a felony is all right

indicators.note: among says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next two

explanation.surface: Crooks' morality: in their circle, committing a serious crime is perfectly acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe means unharmed or out of danger, so someone who is safe is all right.

clue.text: See 2
Pull bird, abandoning the first pigeon

indicators.note: abandoning the first means the opening letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: to drag is to pull
a loon is a diving bird, the North American name for a diver

explanation.surface: A wildlife instruction to pull a bird away from the first pigeon.
explanation.walkthrough: Pull bird reads like attracting a partner, but the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: The dragoon is a breed of fancy domestic pigeon, related to the carrier.

clue.text: See 23
